risk_if_not_implemented: Without Obligation To Inform Third-Parties, supplier and External Service Provider (ESP) weaknesses, incidents or failures may propagate into the organization's environment unmanaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Privacy Harm / Unauthorized Processing (R-IP-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Information Sharing With Third Parties
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to disclose Personal Data (PD) to third-parties only for the purposes identified in the data privacy notice and with the implicit or explicit consent of the data subject.
compensating_control_1.justification: Information Sharing With Third Parties (PRI-16) provides third-party oversight that compensates for the absence of Obligation To Inform Third-Parties (PRI-42) by extending security obligations contractually and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct control. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Sensitive / Regulated Data Sharing Decisions
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a process to assist users in making information sharing decisions to ensure data is appropriately protected.
compensating_control_2.justification: Sensitive / Regulated Data Sharing Decisions (DCH-08.1) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Obligation To Inform Third-Parties (PRI-42) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
